references.text: Describes the same event (the exit from the ark) and confirms the continuity of God's preservation of all animal groups.
Connects God's command to go out and fill the earth (8:17) with the fulfillment that all animals have indeed gone out (9:10).
Creates a theological framework around the flood by comparing the entry (7:14) and exit (9:10) of the same animal groups.
Uses the same list of animal groups to sharply distinguish between those who perished in judgment (7:21) and those who were saved (9:10).
Confirms the continuity of salvation: everything was destroyed except those in the ark (7:23), and now the same groups are saved and outside (9:10).
9:10 establishes the presence of the animals that are the object of fear and submission in 9:2, showing the covenant in action.
Confirms that both clean and unclean animals mentioned at the entry (7:8) were also saved at the exit (9:10).
Creates a parallel between the original creation (1:24) and the restoration of creation after the flood (9:10).
9:10 is the concrete fulfillment of God's command in 6:19 to preserve all animal groups in the ark.
